_comment: Instantly campaign definition for the OryonIQ reach-engine pilot (id 77b2cd80-5bf2-4656-8857-b310858d5a77, PAUSED). {{personalization}} is filled per-lead from the engine's opener; {{sendrPageUrl}} is the lead's own Sendr page, supplied per-lead as a TOP-LEVEL custom_variable (nested inside `payload` it is silently discarded and the API still returns 201). 4-step sequence landing roughly day 0 / 3 / 7 / 13. COPY REWRITTEN 2026-08-29 after the user read a real send and said: 'that's not at all saying what we want to reach, i didn't feel like reading it, and with reading also i didn't understand what the email is mostly about.' Three causes, all structural: (1) the subject was 'quick one, {{firstName}}' which carries no information at all; (2) the opener recited market news, so the email opened on Pentagon policy instead of on the reader; (3) step 1 variant A had NO ASK - it ended on a link and a signature, so there was nothing to reply to. Every step now runs reader -> plain-words offer -> specific artefact -> one small ask. STEPS 2-4 ARE NOW FINISHED COPY - the [[!! ... !!]] placeholder blocks are gone. They were blocked on two disputed claims and BOTH are now dropped everywhere rather than resolved: the copy no longer says federal set-asides are opening (that does not follow from the CMMC Phase II suspension) and no longer claims pre-RFP alerting, NAICS filtering or SDB matching (none of which appear on oryoniq.com - see oryoniq-product-features.md). Everything asserted now maps to a line in that feature list: contract award data, teaming pairs, LinkedIn profile mapping into decision-makers, and the free tier. Step 2-4 subjects are deliberately EMPTY so the follow-ups thread under step 1. The step-1 page sentence is mirrored by engine.py assemble_email(), the n8n 'Assemble + Report' node and the VIO-sendr-generate-page ROUTES map - sync-routes.py enforces it, so change all of them together or the page and the email argue different cases to the same prospect. The two step-1 variants deliberately share their CTA sentence AND their ask, and differ ONLY in the offer paragraph — that is the A/B question (plain statement of what OryonIQ shows vs. the 'your opportunity feed does not cover this' framing). Testing four changes at once tells you nothing about which one moved the number, and sync-routes.py's cta-sentence check refuses to run at all while the variants word the CTA differently. BLOCK ORDER is greeting / opener / offer / ASK / page link / sign-off. The ask sits BEFORE the link on purpose: the question is the real call to action and the page is the lower-commitment alternative for someone not ready to book. It is also the only order the three consumers can share — the n8n preview omits the page sentence it cannot fill and sync-routes.py splices it back immediately before the sign-off, so an ask placed after the link cannot be represented there. COMPLIANCE FOOTER added 2026-08-30 to every step: a valid physical postal address and an opt-out, both required by CAN-SPAM 7704(a)(5) and absent from all 10 bodies until now. The opt-out is reply-based, not a merge tag, because the reply route is already wired to the Suppression tab and proven, while an unverified tag can reach a prospect as a literal token.
